feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/communications leadership. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with tighter structure, more outcome-focused metrics, and reduced duplication across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is credible and shows increasing scope across web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Strong domain fit: public-sector, advocacy, Drupal, analytics, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced throughout.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with good specificity in platforms, tools, and project examples.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (conversion gains, engagement growth, efficiency improvements, cost savings, adoption rates).  
- Simplify structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would reduce repetition and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Fix style consistency: punctuation and formatting vary. Examples: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “problem-solving” vs. “decision-making” is fine, but keep hyphenation conventions consistent; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” may look stylistically inconsistent unless intentional. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear public-sector relevance, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one or two concrete signals of scale would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with sharper, outcome-oriented language tied to enterprise scope.
- Add a concrete scale cue from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Streamline the second sentence to reduce list-like density and improve readability.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web and communications systems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content experiences across complex platforms serving large audiences and distributed publishing teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The current intro closely mirrors the subtitle and skills sections; avoid turning it into another keyword list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording; e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping items to reduce list fatigue and sharpen positioning.
- Prioritize the strongest, most distinctive areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integration, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” is already well covered in the header and multiple NACo roles.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” and “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” closely repeat both the header and Topline Skills sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and AI chat”).
- Add 1 concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible for 1–2 projects.
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and keep punctuation/structure consistent across all entries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent roles; consider reframing as “Selected projects” with sharper implementation or outcome detail.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; keep it, as it adds variety beyond the web/platform themes.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and name the organization if possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-focused lines, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, including downloadable member toolkits and reusable content structures.
- Improved enterprise web operations by streamlining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-channel governance.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift, search success, or publishing efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level or make the footer examples more specific.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the summary and NACo role—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most senior-level achievements without repeating responsibilities covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify newsletter audience, social growth/engagement, studio output, reporting efficiency, or governance improvements.
- Trim generic phrasing like “strengthened” and “improving strategic decision-making”; replace with specifics such as reduced reporting time, standardized publishing workflows, or increased in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise oversight and scale.
- Video-program language may duplicate earlier NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy, program and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper, outcome-oriented phrases:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and mission-driven messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and storytelling
- Keep wording parallel; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” styles inconsistently.
- If space allows, consider “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect seniority and systems leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header and Core Competencies; consider keeping only one public-sector/advocacy reference across summary skills.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize recent strengths tied to current/most recent work.

Suggested edit:

- Replace vague terms like “technical execution” with clearer value language such as “platform delivery” or “web implementation.”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented modifier: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- Most platform/tool names repeat the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version higher-level.

Suggested edit:

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” is already covered in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact framing.

Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent operational leadership rather than generic task terms.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section almost exactly. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or add light context on level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, high-value platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or remove if only occasional use.
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than a raw list: **CMS platforms: Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages**
- Consider aligning with recent experience by making Drupal the clear lead platform, since it is central to current consulting and NACo work.
- Keep naming consistent with other sections; avoid repeating the exact same five-platform list elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- **GitHub Pages** may feel out of step with the senior enterprise/public-sector positioning unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers unless they matter technically; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- If accurate, add scope or level in parentheses to increase credibility, e.g., “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment automation).”
- Consider renaming the heading to **Front-End, Integrations & Deployment** to sound more senior and less like entry-level coding.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if that section has room.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more implementation-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems used to build/coordinate workflows, not just collaboration apps.
- Split core automation tools from project-management tools for clarity and seniority.
- Suggested rewrite: **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello  
  **Collaboration & Team Operations:** Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If accurate, replace one or two generic tools with higher-value descriptors: “Airtable workflow design,” “cross-platform automations,” or “project intake and editorial planning systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack, Teams, and Basecamp are lower-impact than automation platforms; consider dropping one or more if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale or use case, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email campaign execution, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications**
- If accurate, add one qualifier tied to recent work: **supporting high-volume newsletters and advocacy/member engagement programs**
- Keep only the strongest/recent tools first; if one was used lightly or long ago, consider dropping it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email bullets; avoid repeating newsletter scale here unless you remove it from experience bullets.
- “Engagement” is vague; if no CRM/community platform detail is added, the current title may overpromise.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a sharper capabilities list and emphasize methods/tools over broad concepts.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with more specific capability phrasing: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting”
- Consider swapping “SEO” for “SEO analysis” or “technical SEO” to make it skill-based rather than a discipline label.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “executive dashboards” for stronger business relevance.
- If truthful, add one higher-signal analytics implementation skill such as “event tracking strategy,” “conversion measurement,” or “data visualization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this version tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating explanatory detail here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Tighten scope and use stronger verbs: “streamlined workflows across web, email, social and video” instead of “strengthening workflows.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, streamlined publishing workflows across web, email, social and video, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day oversight and coaching for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already emphasized in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around distinct contributions so it doesn’t overlap too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business value tied to programs/policy support.
- Split into 2 concise bullets and emphasize ownership verbs: launched, managed, produced, supported.
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audiences served, research deliverables, or programs supported.

Example rewrite
- Supported county innovation and research initiatives that informed NACo program development and policy work.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production, while also producing supporting digital and multimedia content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that repeats later web/video leadership roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; stronger management evidence appears in later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a generic software inventory than a targeted capability statement. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery,” so this item should emphasize tools only and keep production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or tighten to a pure tools line: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want a bit more specificity, use grouped phrasing: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- Move non-tool items out of this entry: **livestream studio workflows** and **podcast production** fit better under competencies or experience bullets, where they can be tied to outcomes.
